newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cities under pollution alert for second day.
newsitem.headline: French cities under pollution alert for second day.

text.p: Paris police lowered speed limits and urged drivers to leave their cars at home on Wednesday as the French capital tried to cut back car emissions to avoid a pollution crisis during a summer heat wave.

Air quality was still bad after officials in Paris, Lille, Lyon and Strasbourg issued an air pollution alert on Tuesday as a combination of heat, sunlight, car exhausts and a lack of wind pushed pollution to health-threatening levels
Paris offered free parking in residential areas to get commuters to leave their cars there and Strasbourg laid on extra buses and trams to lure more commuters to public transport.
Public health officials have urged the elderly, small children and people with respiratory problems to limit their physical activity during the alert.

But pollution levels were measured at "level two," the midpoint on the official scale and one step below the "level three" alert that would require curbs on private cars and free public transport in the large cities.
Speed limits were lowered by 20 kmh on Paris highways and drivers in the city were urged to accelerate slowly and not leave engines running while the car is standing.
The Paris pollution monitoring authority Airparif said the alerts could continue for the next few days as midday temperatures hover over the 30 degrees centigrade mark.
The pollution alert has also triggered a debate about environmental policy between the new Socialist government and the former conservative administration.

Corinne Lepage, the former environment minister, said she hoped her leftist successor, Greens leader Dominique Voynet, would "have the political courage" to restrict private cars although level three had not been reached.
Lepage wants to allow private cars only on alternate days, according to the numbers on their licence plates.
But the Environment Ministry did not opt for such limits, promising instead a long-term change in transport policy with a "green vignette" allowing low-polluting cars to circulate.
Cars that fail a clean exhaust test would be barred from the roads during a pollution alert.
"Dominique Voynet considers this system more educational," a ministry spokesman said, adding a decree to this effect would be made later this year.
